deploy-bot: Pager: Canary alert — svc-inference-canary showing bursty 5xx spikes (p95 latency + error rate). Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/alerts/1769999992 :rotating_light:
maria (oncall): Paging in. seeing short 503 bursts ~6x in last minute in us-west1, not long enough to auto-rollback. I will triage.
Lee (sre): On it. Can you grab a quick curl to /health? I want to see pattern across pods.
maria (oncall): ran `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://svc-canary.us-west1/health` — responses flip 200 / 503 intermittently, roughly every 8-12s.
Rahul: I pulled kube logs — I see OOMKilled entries on gpunode-17 around the same timestamps. Pushed logs to /logs/canary/1769999992 and notified #eng-runtime.
Sam (product): Any customer-facing errors yet? Need to coordinate comms if this affects SLAs.
Jess (support): 3 customer reports in last 10m about slow/failed responses. No data-loss reported. Marking as P2 for CS.
maria (oncall): Proposed immediate plan: 1) freeze rollout 2) flip canary routing flag off (route traffic to stable pool) 3) drain canary pods 4) promote previous revision (v1.42) as rollback 5) run smoke + perf checks 6) monitor 30m then update status page. Thoughts?
Lee (sre): +1. Suggest also snapshot current pod logs + heap profiles before drain. Command to flip flag: `curl -X POST https://flags.redwood/api/flip -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"flag":"canary_route","value":false}'`
maria (oncall): Executing flag flip now.
deploy-bot: Action: feature flag `canary_route` set to false by maria (oncall). Traffic shifting off canary -> stable pool.
Rahul: Observing traffic shift. Canary error rate trending down to ~0.2%. Starting rollback artifact: `deployctl rollback --service svc-inference --to v1.42 --mode manual`
Lee (sre): K8s drain: `kubectl drain svc-canary-pool --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — running now. Also kicking off smoke tests: `make smoke-test`
maria (oncall): Smoke tests passing on stable pool. Perf and correctness quick checks look good.
Sam (product): Drafted CS update: "We've routed traffic away from the canary due to intermittent errors and restored stable instances. We're monitoring and will post updates." Jess, can you push to status.redwood?
Jess (support): Posted status page update and replied to affected customers with the CS template. Two tickets marked as monitored, one closed.
Rahul: Keeping a 30m watch on latency and 5xx. If stable for that window we'll resolve and run a follow-up postmortem. Collected heap dumps and scaling events for root cause.
maria (oncall): Incident record created. Tagging eng-runtime for deep dive into memory/autoscaling behavior.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created: "canary stutter — manual rollback executed". Assigned to eng-runtime.
Lee (sre): Quick hypothesis: autoscaler scaleDown agressive threshold + cold-starty workloads caused transient OOMs under burst. Captured prometheus graphs and pod lifecycles to validate.
Sam (product): Thanks team. Maria, handing ongoing watch to Lee. I'll own customer comms post-mitigation.
maria (oncall): Leaving page to Lee. Will assemble notes for postmortem. Thanks all.
